biggest_gap.title: Round 12's gap is still open: a manager of company X can close a branch of company Y through a write path that bypasses SaveChanges, and every gate passes
biggest_gap.detail: The company-role gate (tests/Erp.Gates.Tests/G2/CompanyRoleRecords.cs) is byte-for-byte unchanged since round 12. It still sends company Y's records only G1WriteOracle.Valid bodies, in which every boolean is true. Its named writes change only tradeLicenceNumber and city. So no write path that runs only when a boolean changes is ever exercised against Y: isActive false (closing a branch or a company), arabicLegalNameRequired, allBranches. The product's second layer, the per-company permission check in ModuleDbContext.SaveChanges, also guards only tracked SaveChanges writes. ExecuteUpdate and ExecuteDelete bypass it, and the codebase already uses them, for example CompanyAccessRules.cs:88 and identity's bulk endpoints. I replanted round 12's P1e class in BranchEndpoints.Update: closing a branch with one ExecuteUpdate before the PermitsCompany check. All 172 gates passed. Live, the Dubai LLC's manager closed a branch of the free-zone entity, where she holds only Read-only. Closing a branch stops everyone working there. This is the 'accountant in the mainland LLC, read-only in the JAFZA entity' set-up that UAE groups use. Suggested fix: 1) For every endpoint, build each Y record's body from the record as read, then change each field one at a time (booleans and enums included) to another valid value. Send each variant, with X records as controls, and compare snapshots after each change. 2) Make the second layer cover set-based writes, for example a database-side company-permission check or a reviewed ban on ExecuteUpdate/ExecuteDelete over ICompanyOwned sets outside reviewed files. 3) Add 'closing a Y branch through a boolean-only ExecuteUpdate path' to the gate self-tests.
biggest_gap.evidence: plants/plant-batchB-P1-P2.diff (P1 hunk) applied at b033a15f; the planted file is plants/P1-BranchEndpoints-planted.cs.txt. Run `ERP_TEST_PASSWORD_ITERATIONS=10000 dotnet test tests/Erp.Gates.Tests -c Release --filter "Load!=Timing&Process!=self-http&Process!=self-company&Process!=self-noninterference&FullyQualifiedName!~Erp.Gates.Tests.SelfTests"`: 172/172 pass (plants/plant-batchB-gates.log). For the live check, start the planted stack with ERP_PROJECT=x ERP_HTTP_PORT=20270 ERP_DB_PORT=20271 ERP_SEED_VOLUME=2000 ./erp up, then run node plants/P1-P2-live.mjs http://localhost:20270. Signed in as accountant@alnoor.example and working in ALN-DXB, she sends PUT /api/tenancy/branches/{DAFZ-OF of ALN-FZE}. With city changed it answers 403 permissionNotHeldInCompany. With isActive:false it answers 200, and the branch goes from active true to false (plants/P1-P2-live.log). Gate source: CompanyRoleRecords.cs is unchanged (git diff 0baa6c6a50 b033a15f -- tests/Erp.Gates.Tests/G2/CompanyRoleRecords.cs is empty).

other_findings: Round 12's biggest gap has not been worked on. Since round 12 the piece branch carries only the UAE phone-length rule, its documented pattern, a switch-company driver set-up change and a decision record. The company-role gate files are unchanged.
